name: Qutbism
summary: Qutbism is the Sunni Islamist doctrine of Sayyid Qutb. It holds that sovereignty and legislation belong to God alone, that societies not ruled by sharia live in a new jahiliyyah, and that a committed vanguard must break from them and establish Islamic order through preaching and, where needed, jihad. It rejects nationalism, secularism, democracy, socialism and capitalism as man-made systems, while urging social justice under divine law.
scope: Based on Qutb's Milestones (1964) and his earlier writings such as Social Justice in Islam, as described by scholarship. It covers the Qutbist core, not the later jihadist movements (al-Qaeda, IS) or the Muslim Brotherhood mainstream that disputed his takfir.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His redistributive Social Justice in Islam implies public provision for the needy, so universal healthcare is inferred; healthcare itself is not addressed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on just distribution of wealth and dignity for the poor; wage law is not discussed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He wrote against capitalism (The Struggle between Islam and Capitalism) and treats economics as subject to divine law, but accepts trade and private enterprise; inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: He accepted private property within sharia limits and also state redistribution; no source gives a view on nationalizing industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from his redistributive reading of zakat and criticism of concentrated wealth in Social Justice in Islam.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not addressed; he rejects class-based organization but supports protecting the poor.

property-fundamental.rationale: Islam permits property but under divine law and for the common good, so it can be limited; critics cite his reported support for confiscation in some cases.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from his demand that economic life follow divine law and avoid exploitation such as usury.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mutual social security and obligatory giving are part of his Islamic social order, so cutting welfare as dependency-forming is unlikely to be his view.

worker-ownership.rationale: He rejected socialism and class-based schemes as non-Islamic; worker ownership is inferred as foreign to his program.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; he supported a strong Islamic state but was himself a victim of Nasserist state security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Sharia prohibits intoxicants, and Milestones credits Islam with abolishing drinking and gambling; legal recreational drugs would be a jahili licence.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; he would restrict speech against Islam but also demanded freedom to preach, so no clear answer.

strong-leader.rationale: After 1952 he backed a 'just dictatorship' that would bypass politics for virtuous ends, though the ruler remains bound by sharia.

state-harmful.rationale: He wanted an Islamic state enforcing sharia and a vanguard to establish it; Islamic order requires authority and power.

empower-police-military.rationale: He valued Muslim power to defend and spread Islam, but disliked the secular Egyptian security state that tortured him.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: He condemned Western sexual permissiveness and held sharia forbids fornication; he listed such practices among jahiliyyah.

decide-locally.rationale: He held sovereignty and law are God's and universal, not local; one Islamic order should apply, though administration could be local.

rehabilitation.rationale: He treats sharia punishments as divinely prescribed; rehabilitation over punishment is inferred as secondary.

traditional-family.rationale: He treated the family as part of the divinely ordered way of life and held that men manage women's affairs; Western family disintegration is part of his critique.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sharia forbids same-sex relations and he derided Western moral looseness; no explicit text, but central to a sharia order.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from classical sharia's protection of life and his rejection of permissive Western morals.

more-religion-public.rationale: Islam must govern every area of life and state, and he denounced secularism as oppressive.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He held all races equal under God's banner, but programs to redress historical injustice are not addressed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He held the Quran makes men managers of women's affairs and regarded sex roles as divinely ordained.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He called national and ethnic loyalties jahili 'low associations'; what is to be preserved is Islamic culture, not national.

gradual-change.rationale: Milestones calls for a vanguard that breaks with jahili society and dismantles its structures, rejecting reform within existing institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Man-made international bodies exercise legislative authority that Qutb reserves to God; he saw them as jahili.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; trade is permitted in Islam but his economics is anti-capitalist.

nation-first.rationale: He held the homeland's soil has no value in itself and loyalty is to faith; he also opposed jahili global order, so only a weak No.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He cites the Quranic call to fight for the oppressed and frames jihad as liberation of people, though from Islamic, not human-rights, premises.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; unity of believers across borders but not open borders for all.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; no environmental teaching in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He held Western civilization materially advanced but spiritually bankrupt; only submission to God solves humanity's problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power was far outside Qutb's concerns, and nothing in Milestones points either way, so this is a neutral low-confidence answer.

revolution-justified.rationale: Milestones calls on a vanguard to overthrow jahili order, by force if needed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority rests with divine law; neither experts nor public decide. No clear answer.

central-planning.rationale: He rejected socialism as non-Islamic and favored a divine-law economy with private property.

socialized-markets.rationale: He rejected socialism and public-ownership schemes as man-made systems.

land-value-tax.rationale: Qutb wrote no fiscal theory of land taxation; his economics centres on zakat, the usury ban and just distribution, so no stance is inferable.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sharia fixes inheritance shares, so heavy taxation of inheritance is not part of the divinely set scheme.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; zakat gives to the needy but is not unconditional.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not discussed in Milestones; his economic writings target capitalism and usury rather than tariffs, so I answer neutral.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He wanted economic life under divine law but did not describe state investment planning, so there is no basis for a stance.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred from his concern over concentrated wealth in pre-Islamic Mecca and his just-distribution theme.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Utopian abolition is a Marxist idea he rejected; Islam as practised regulates trade and wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed, though he opposes usury.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He rejected class-based arrangements as divisive and prefers divine law; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wanted an Islamic order under sharia led initially by a vanguard, not a standing party state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He held the ruler is chosen by the community and obeyed only while upholding sharia; hereditary kingship is not endorsed.

democracy-best.rationale: He held assemblies with absolute power to legislate are un-Islamic since legislation belongs to God alone.

direct-votes.rationale: Voting on laws gives humans a legislative right that Milestones reserves to God.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based rule and man-made political foundations are both rejected.

right-to-secede.rationale: He cared for the unity of the Muslim community and rejected nation-state boundaries as legitimate; secession is inferred negative.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rulers qualify by piety and by adherence to sharia and must be men, but no doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: He justified jihad, including offensive jihad, to remove jahili systems.

war-builds-character.rationale: He treats jihad as a struggle that tests and purifies the believer, though not as a general claim about nations.

separate-church-state.rationale: He denounced secularism and held Islam is a total system governing state and society.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Sovereignty and legislation belong to God alone, with the Quran and sharia as the law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Justice and defense belong to the Islamic state under divine law.

military-superiority.rationale: Milestones stresses power as necessary to remove obstacles to Islam; inferred for Muslim states.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Race, colour and language are called low associations; the community is bound by faith alone.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Milestones explicitly lists class struggle among corrupt theories; Islam unites classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He held just distribution and mutual responsibility, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Qutb frames land as valuable only where God's authority is established, and he never addressed indigenous peoples' claims; neutral by default.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He viewed Western imperialism as an attack on Islam; reparations are inferred, not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: The community is based on faith, across races and nations, and he rejected nation-state divisions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He criticized materialism and individualism and urged submission to God over personal interests.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Obedience and duty to God and the community are central; Islam is submission.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is absent from his sources; creation is God's, but he drew no political conclusion about nature's own value.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from a traditional Islamic view; not addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He faulted Western spiritual bankruptcy but did not reject industry or science.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He wanted society reordered around divine law, not disruption for technology; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from traditional Islamic limits on altering creation.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government is God's law applied by a believing ruler; delegation to algorithms would be another man-made authority.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1960s writer; his sources give no principle that settles privacy against state power.

restore-past-order.rationale: He called for re-establishing Islam as in the Prophet's generation, treating the present as pre-Islamic ignorance.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy must follow divine law, not results.

direct-action.rationale: His program is a vanguard that preaches and fights, not electoral politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not clearly addressed; he holds both pious method and force.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; inferred, since his order is a developed Islamic society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of Marxism and acceptance of distinct roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He favored just distribution and care for the needy, but also reward for work under sharia.

production-for-use.rationale: He did not discuss production aims; he condemned usury and exploitation but accepted trade, so I leave it neutral.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He condemned usury, not trade profit as such, and rejected Marxist analysis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejected class rule and communism as jahili systems.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of socialism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He denounced imperialism but rejected the Marxist theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: Zakat is a religious duty enforced by the Islamic order.

harm-principle.rationale: God's law restricts conduct beyond harm to others, including drink and sexual conduct.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Duty and submission to God come first, not individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Jihad is an obligation, so general service is inferred acceptable.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; the community's authority is not a market of exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state exists to apply divine law, not serve customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: He wrote of freedom for man from servitude and of Islam satisfying material needs.

media-academia-power.rationale: His sources do not weigh media and universities against elected officials, though he distrusted secular elites and defeated scholars; neutral.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He rejected race as a basis of worth.

organic-representation.rationale: He rejected party and parliamentary politics but proposed no guild or family representation, so adherents have no settled view here.

total-state.rationale: Sharia covers belief, administration, morality and knowledge; the state enforces a total way of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: He called for a revival from jahiliyyah, though of the Muslim community, not a nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He called for offensive jihad to spread Islam's authority; the aim is Islamic order, not national territory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He held no authority of one man over another; loyalty is to God, though allegiance to Islamic leaders is expected.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from his stress on freeing people from servitude to others.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He insisted that Islamic sources alone give truth and that jahili sources are corrupting.

universal-morality.rationale: He held divine truth is universal for all peoples, but known by revelation rather than reason.

single-common-good.rationale: One divine system defines the good for all, rather than balancing group interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He portrayed Jews as enemies of Islam and rejected Western-backed claims on Muslim lands.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of ethnic-national claims.

revive-national-language.rationale: Arabic matters to Islam as the language of the Quran, but he rejected national identity as a political basis, so the claim as worded is not his.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of democratic sovereignty and socialist schemes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding mechanisms are not addressed; he wanted education grounded in Islam, which does not decide for or against vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is not in Milestones or his social writing; the usury ban touches debt but gives no stance on stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic life is subject to divine law, not freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: He emphasized the believing ruler's piety, though sharia law is enforced.

national-self-determination.rationale: He rejected nation-states as a Western notion and put God's authority above national choice.

force-without-un.rationale: He held jihad needs no human-made body's approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Revelation, not reason, is the sole source of guidance.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Muslim and non-Muslim status in the Islamic state differ.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from Islamic work ethic; not addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: He rejected class struggle and held society united under faith.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He wanted to restore the heritage of Islam, so sacrificing inherited culture contradicts his aim.

dominated-front.rationale: He urged Muslims to resist Western domination as a faith war.

workers-nation.rationale: He rejected both national and class loyalties.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He held men manage women's affairs and said the ruler must be male.

ban-interest.rationale: Milestones notes usury as prohibited by Islam and as a sign of pre-Islamic injustice.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Milestones says people of any race or colour are equal under the banner of God and treats race as a low association.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He viewed class analysis as corrupt and the state as an instrument for divine law.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is outside his texts, so I record a neutral answer with no inference.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Membership in his community is by faith, not nationality, and immigration to national cultures is not discussed; neutral.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of his teaching; he rejects race-based reasoning.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party-based parliamentary politics is itself man-made legislation.

national-mission.rationale: Islam's mission is universal; the model is the Muslim community, not one state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He saw male management as divinely ordained, not as a system of disadvantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He held rulers who do not apply sharia are jahili and oppressive.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from Islamic respect for life; not addressed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He suffered torture under Nasser; accountability is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Islamic state governs all life, not just security.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He called race a low association and described equality of all races.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Law is uniform for rulers and ruled and all races are equal, though belief grades status.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He rejected socialism altogether as a man-made system and never engaged this internal Marxist debate.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from his hostility to imperialism and Zionism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: He held sharia is the law for the Muslim community and non-Muslims may not make law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He backed free preaching and also apostasy limits.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No basis in Islamic law; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Islamic education and religion shape the state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority comes from God; the ruler is chosen by the community and obeyed while upholding sharia.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not addressed in his work; neutral.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Faith and cooperation under divine law drive the Islamic order.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A sharia order would outlaw parties seeking to impose man-made law.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: His central claim is that obedience to God frees people from servitude to other humans.

separated-powers.rationale: Authority is under sharia, not balanced.

vanguard-party.rationale: He demanded a disciplined vanguard, but of believers, not of the working class, and rejected class politics; it is split on the literal wording.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His Social Justice in Islam is a redistributive work, and Milestones criticizes pre-Islamic concentration of wealth and neglect of the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not addressed; his property views are tied to sharia, which does not settle the question.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor action is not discussed in his sources, and I cannot infer a position from his rejection of class struggle alone.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He blamed injustice and bad distribution for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He held that faith unites diverse peoples.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Office goes to qualified believers; lottery is not Islamic.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He backed a just dictatorship and militant defence of the movement; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing is not discussed; classical Islamic jurists were divided on it, so adherents have no settled view.

party-controls-media.rationale: He wanted media and culture shaped by Islam, but control by a ruling party is not part of his model; neutral.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party commanding the army is not part of his model.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Membership is by faith, not residence.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of officials is not addressed in his sources, and elected representatives are not part of his system anyway.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The vanguard is a disciplined group under a strict code.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Secular supranational unions are man-made sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Islamic ruler leads the community's forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: No church hierarchy in Sunni Islam; not applicable.

clerical-rule.rationale: Qutb, a lay writer without traditional training, put authority in sharia and the ruler.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist class thesis is foreign to him.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He criticized jazz and moral looseness and held the Islamic order protects morality.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits assume an elected presidency, which Qutb did not discuss; the ruler is bound by sharia, not terms.

recall-officials.rationale: A ruler who departs from sharia loses the right to obedience.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He opposed Western domination yet wanted Muslim power; alliance policy itself is not addressed, so neutral.

people-in-arms.rationale: He valued every believer's duty of jihad, but no text endorses replacing a professional army with a militia; neutral.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Milestones does not compare rural and urban life; his moral criticism targets Western materialism, not cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He sought Muslim unity across borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed, though he disparaged defeated Muslim scholars.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He held Islam above all jahili civilizations.

death-penalty.rationale: Sharia provides capital punishment, and he stressed that its penalties must be applied.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He condemned sexual mixing and Western gender norms.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from Quranic creation; not addressed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Sharia rules on modesty and he condemned Western sexual licence.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Community membership is by faith, not descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is outside his sources, and he treated language as a low association; I leave it neutral.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He wanted one sharia for the state, but non-Muslim communities' exemption is not addressed in the sources I read; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He held that society must follow divine law and the believing community.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from usury ban and anti-imperialism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He held that true freedom requires rejecting all human systems, including economic.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making by a human assembly is a claim to legislate that belongs to God.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Economic development strategy is not addressed; his priorities are religious order, not growth, so neutral.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from zakat and social justice.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from his stress on Muslim power; anachronistic.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He said the ruler is chosen by the community but gave no mechanism, so neither direct nor indirect election is his stated view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Modern central banking is absent from his work; his only monetary doctrine is the ban on usury.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Lands once under Islam are not to be surrendered; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is held under divine law and social obligations.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He rejected Soviet communism as jahili, not on this ground.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is not addressed in his texts; neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: He held the Muslim community defends its members.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from his view of imperial seizure.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He held Islam's law governs the state.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: His ruler governs under sharia and is not a ceremonial symbol, but party politics are not discussed either; neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the unity of the community.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy within a larger state is not discussed; he wanted a single Islamic order, though local administration is not excluded.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He held no human has authority over another and sovereignty is God's.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax design is not in his sources; zakat is a fixed-rate levy, but that does not settle income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: He thought society's system shapes people, yet he also held a divine nature (fitra); his sources do not settle the question.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rulers are obeyed only while following sharia.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Authority is divine law, not mixed.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring a leader as embodiment of the nation conflicts with God's sole sovereignty.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in the sources I read; classical sharia rules differ, so I record neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He rejected socialism and class struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; critics said he proposed redistribution.

refugee-return.rationale: He did not address refugee rights; a low-confidence positive follows from his view that Muslim lands should be defended and held.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He rejected nationality as a basis for claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from classical sharia; not read in the sources.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed; he opposed nation-state divisions but also usury-based finance, leaving no clear stance.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He called language and ancestry low associations.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine he did not address; he rejected socialism but did urge a strong, armed Islamic community against hostile surroundings.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Qutb rejects nationalism and wants one Islamic order under sharia; autonomous minority institutions inside a non-Islamic state are inferred to be refused, not addressed directly.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from his call for believers to separate from jahili society rather than seek equal rights within it; he does not discuss founding a homeland.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Milestones rejects Marxist materialism and holds that belief and submission to God, not economic conditions, drive social change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from Social Justice in Islam, which attacks concentrated wealth and usury; competition law is not discussed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from his critique of capitalism and usury-based finance; bailouts are not addressed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to God alone, so no majority may legislate against sharia and courts apply divine law, not majority will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He defended distinct roles for men and women and criticised Western gender mixing, so quotas for equal representation would be rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of nationalist blocs in favour of Muslim unity; autarky is not addressed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from his social-justice concern for workers and the poor; trade agreements are not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from his stress on spiritual motive and duty to God over material gain; not directly addressed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Milestones calls for a vanguard that breaks from jahili society and uses jihad to remove the obstacles to Islamic order rather than waiting.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from his insistence on equality before God and rejection of class and race privilege; titles are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Qutb rejects nationalism but wants education centred on the Islamic community and its history, which he treats as the civilisation's own.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Milestones holds that Western civilisation is bankrupt and its leadership at an end, and Qutb rejects domination of one people over another.

patriotic-education.rationale: Qutb rejects nationalism and loyalty to flags and homelands as jahili ties; loyalty is owed to God and the faith community only.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: Qutb held that faith alone, not race or colour, may distinguish people, so privileges based on race are illegitimate.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Qutb condemned usury and rejected capitalism as man-made, which suggests opposition to interest-based private money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: Qutb treats capitalism as a jahili system, but he does not argue from a Marxist collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: Qutb rejects nationalism and states' claims to regional spheres; his aim is an Islamic order, not a revived national empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: Qutb never addressed development strategy; he rejects dependence on jahili systems but does not call for breaking trade ties.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: Qutb frames conflict as faith against jahiliyyah, not as a class division that rich-country workers profit from.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: Qutb's social justice under divine law binds owners by sharia, so an unrestricted freedom to refuse and discriminate on any ground is rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Qutb holds that sovereignty and law belong to God alone, so a man-made bill of rights that limits government is itself a jahili authority.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Qutb condemned Western imperial domination of Muslim lands, though he rejected nation-state borders as such; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Qutb wanted a ruler chosen by the community's consent and consultation under sharia, not a hereditary tyrant; scholarship on this is mixed.

minority-veto.rationale: Divine law binds all believers, and the vanguard follows God's rule, not majority or minority consent; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A ruler who does not rule by God's law has lost legitimacy, and the vanguard works to overthrow him.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Sovereignty and legislation belong to God alone, so a parliament cannot be the supreme lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the Islamic tradition of mercy to animals; Qutb did not address it directly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from Islamic law permitting animals for food with humane slaughter; Qutb gives no separate statement.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Qutb's Social Justice in Islam makes mutual responsibility and zakat a duty of the wealthy toward the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Qutb calls for an active vanguard that works to establish God's order, so withdrawal from public affairs is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Qutb condemned Western media and culture as promoting jahili values and moral decay; this does not mirror a Marxist reproduction thesis, so inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Qutb held that jahili systems keep people submitting to man-made authority through culture and education as well as force; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Qutb criticised capitalism and Western domination of Muslim lands; inferred from that critique.

native-born-offices.rationale: Qutb rejected nationalism and held that the bond of belief, not birth or homeland, defines the community.

party-own-road.rationale: Qutb rejected socialism and rejected national roads; only the Islamic way counts, so the question lies outside his framework; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the vanguard's call for independence from jahili systems and criticism of dependence on the West.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Qutb denied that homeland and territory are the basis of loyalty and rejected nationalist claims; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Qutb held that race, ancestry and territory create no claim to leadership; only belief in God's law does.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Qutb treats no man-made ideology as a founding value; the founding law is sharia; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Qutb condemned both communism and the Western systems as jahiliyyah, but the totalitarianism framing is not his; adherents are split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the statement is outside Qutb's writing, and nothing he wrote supports denying slavery's role.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Qutb's tawhid-centred ethos opposes honouring figures of jahili society; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Qutb held complementary gender roles with the home as a woman's primary task; equal programmes for men's disadvantage is not his emphasis; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Qutb's complementary gender roles and sharia family law; no statement on the symmetry of violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Qutb rejected man-made Western institutions, including democracy, for a system under God's law.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Qutb was imprisoned and executed by Nasser's officer regime and held rule belongs to God's law, not army; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Qutb held women's primary duty is in the home and did not propose to pay it as labour; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Sovereignty belongs to God alone, so no human assembly or ruler may make law of its own.
missingStatements.rationale: Hakimiyya is the core of Milestones: no sovereignty or law except God's and no authority of one man over another.

missingStatements.text: Armed struggle is justified to remove political systems that stand in the way of a religion being preached and practised.
missingStatements.rationale: Milestones' jihad chapter calls for movement and force to remove the obstacles of jahili political power.

notes: Strands differ on takfir of ordinary Muslims; some Brotherhood defenders say Qutb never declared Muslims apostates. Many answers are inferred because Qutb wrote little on modern policy.
